t: This is Dalston Library, a public library, named after C. L. R. James. James was a Trinidadian historian, journalist, activist and Marxist writer, whose work is influential in postcolonial literature. In 1937 he wrote World Revolution, a history of the Communist International, which stirred debate in Trotskyist circles. In 1938 he wrote The Black Jacobins, about the Haitian Revolution. So a library, a place for books and ideas, carries the name of a writer who spent his life arguing about them.
